reconstructed_theorem_text: Let Omega be measurable, S a pseudometrizable topological space with its Borel measurable structure, F a nonnegative-real-time filtration, and mu a finite measure on Omega. Let X:NNReal x Omega->S be jointly measurable and strongly progressive for F, and let c:NNReal x S->R be measurable. Fix any T in NNReal and p in ENNReal. Suppose there exists a real C such that |c(t,x)|<=C for every nonnegative t<=T and every x in S. Set b(t,omega)=c(t,X(t,omega)). Then b is strongly progressive; every path t->b(t,omega) is integrable for nu_T=comap(NNReal.toReal, Lebesgue restricted to [0,T]); and (omega,t)->b(t,omega) is MemLp with exponent p for mu.prod(nu_T). Neither compactness nor second countability of S is assumed.
objects: Measurable Omega; pseudometrizable Borel space S; filtration F; finite measure mu.
Jointly measurable strongly progressive X, measurable coefficient c and composition b.
Time measure nu_T, product measure mu.prod(nu_T), and swapped process function (omega,t)->b(t,omega).
domains: p is arbitrary ENNReal, including zero and infinity.
The existential bound C is real; the state variable in its bound ranges over all S.
quantifiers: For every given T,p and all other admissible data, assume exists C, forall t<=T, forall x in S, |c(t,x)|<=C.
The bound C is one common constant for all t<=T and states x; the fixed T is outside its existential quantifier.
The conclusion includes forall omega pathwise integrability, and forall horizon i strong progressivity.
assumptions: S is pseudometrizable and Borel measurable.
mu is finite, not necessarily a probability measure.
X is jointly measurable and strongly progressive.
c is measurable, with a uniform bound over all states up to the selected T.
No compactness, second countability, continuity of c, positive T, or lower bound p>=1 is imposed.
conclusion: b is globally strongly progressive: on each initial-time subtype {t<=i}, b is strongly measurable for the time sigma-algebra product F_i.
For every omega, b(.,omega) is nu_T-integrable.
processFunction b is MemLp p with respect to mu.prod(nu_T), for all allowable ENNReal exponents including 0 and infinity.
scopes: The bound hypothesis only concerns the chosen horizon T, while strong progressivity concerns every horizon.
Uniformity in x is over the entire state space, not just observed states or AE states.
Strong progressivity is not a mu-AE property; MemLp uses AE strong measurability.
constant_dependencies: The witness C can depend on c,S and the selected T; no common C for all T is asserted.
No nonnegativity premise on C is stated separately; the inequality itself constrains it whenever the quantified domain is nonempty.
No quantitative MemLp norm bound is in the conclusion.

semantic_checks.totalized_integrals: Explicit Integrable and MemLp predicates, not bare real-integral equalities. The pointwise bounded measurable time paths give genuine integrability.
semantic_checks.ae_pointwise_order: Uniform c-bound and pathwise integrability are pointwise over all states or samples. The AE aspect resides in MemLp only.
semantic_checks.pushforwards: No probability-law map. Supplied definitions fix nu_T as a comap and processTimeMeasure as mu.prod(nu_T), with omega before time.
semantic_checks.interval_orientation: Closed restricted time interval [0,T] on NNReal; no oriented integral.
semantic_checks.exponents: p ranges over all ENNReal: p=0 uses the standard zero-exponent MemLp convention, infinity means essential boundedness, and 0<p<1 is also included.
semantic_checks.compactness: There is deliberately no CompactSpace or SecondCountableTopology hypothesis on S.
semantic_checks.zero_endpoints: T=0 is admitted and nu_0 is zero; the pointwise bound at t=0 remains part of the hypothesis.
